title: Heisenberg Echo Symmetrization for Gate-Insertion Error Mitigation
abstract: Gate insertion (GI) quantum error mitigation replaces involutory gates such as CZ and CX with 2j+1 repetitions of the same gates to nominally amplify noise by the same factor. Analytical and experimental results show that this amplification scaling fails for non-commuting gate noise, as typically encountered in realistic devices. Here we introduce Heisenberg-echo symmetrization (HES), which combines standard GI with an echo inspired by the Heisenberg representation to cancel the leading GI error. In our simulations, HES reduces the absolute fidelity error by one to two orders of magnitude compared with GI. Unlike the more accurate Layered-KIK method, HES is compatible with any hardware and requires only circuit-level access. It enables virtual noise scaling across platforms, potentially reducing sampling overhead substantially. Its agnostic noise amplification also provides full resilience to temporal noise drift. For pure initial states, however, high-rank observables can substantially increase the echo variance relative to non-echoed circuits, whereas rank-one observables incur no additional sampling overhead compared with GI or Layered-KIK. HES is therefore particularly suited to rank-one or nearly rank-one observables.
summary: This paper introduces Heisenberg-echo symmetrization (HES), an advanced quantum error mitigation technique designed to fix the fundamental flaw in standard Gate Insertion (GI) protocols. By incorporating a Heisenberg echo structure, HES cancels leading error terms arising from non-commuting gate noise. This results in substantial fidelity improvements while maintaining hardware compatibility, making it a powerful tool for near-term quantum devices.
main_problem: Gate insertion (GI) quantum error mitigation fails when the noise channel does not commute with the ideal gate, leading to noise distortion rather than simple noise amplification.
main_result: Heisenberg-echo symmetrization (HES) significantly reduces the absolute fidelity error by one to two orders of magnitude compared to standard GI.
method: HES combines standard GI with an echo derived from the Heisenberg representation to analytically cancel the leading error term caused by non-commuting gate noise.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on quantum computation involving noisy gates (e.g., CZ, CX) modeled using Liouville space operators and noise channels.
key_observables: Absolute fidelity error, expectation values of observables $\langle A angle$, and variance $	ext{Var}(A)$.
important_parameters: Mitigation order ($m$), noise strength ($\xi$), and the rank of the observable (HES is best for rank-one observables).
main_assumptions: HES is compatible with any hardware and requires only circuit-level access, although high-rank observables can increase echo variance.

paper_structure: The paper first establishes the failure of GI for non-commuting noise, then introduces HES as a correction mechanism by combining GI with a Heisenberg echo structure, and finally presents simulations comparing HES's error suppression against GI and KIK.
why_interesting: It provides a hardware-agnostic, theoretically grounded improvement over existing quantum error mitigation techniques, which is crucial for scaling quantum computation.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Mean infidelity as a function of the mitigation order m. The results were averaged over 50 random seven-qubit circuits of depth seven (see main text). The Heisenberg echo (HES-blue) outperforms the standard gate insertion (GI-red) protocol. In the weak noise case (a) the HES fidelity for large m is 80 times better than that of GI and in the strong noise case (b) the improvement factor is 30. As expected from theory, the pulse-inverse-based KIK method is more accurate than HES, but HES has the same implementation simplicity and universal compatibility as GI.
